name: Ascendant Grammar
description: Defines the Ascendant's reference-frame role, approved functions, sign modification, ruler delegation, and clause capabilities.

approvedSecondaryVerbs.useWhen: The emphasis is on movement toward experience or environment.
The emphasis is on how the self is situated at the interaction threshold.
The emphasis is on the reference structure organizing perception or response.
The emphasis is on beginning participation in a context.
The emphasis is on observable embodiment or presentation; never as the complete identity.

correctiveVerbs.useRule: Use only when explicit concealment, performance, or defensive presentation evidence exists.
Use only when the reference frame selects or prioritizes incoming information.
Use only when an immediate response is explicitly being described; reaction is not the full angle function.

modifierIntegrationRules: The sign modifies the manner, strategy, pace, or orientation of `orient`.
No sign may replace the Ascendant reference-frame function.
Sign modifiers must remain grammatical components rather than completed descriptions.
rulerIntegrationRules: The Ascendant ruler supplies a planetary function that operates through or organizes the orientation.
The ruler does not replace the Ascendant.
The Ascendant does not become the ruler's planetary verb.
Ruler house position supplies context, not identity.
prohibitedGrammar: A completed rising-sign interpretation inside the angle object

provenance.sourcePolicy: Reference-frame vocabulary only. The Ascendant may orient other functions but may not become a planet, sign, house, personality label, or finished reading.
